lead.headline: United Russia takes a record 355 Duma seats in first wartime vote
lead.dek: Pamfilova reports preliminary results Monday with more than 95% counted; most anti-war candidates were kept off the ballot
body: President Vladimir Putin's United Russia party won a record 355 of the 450 seats in the State Duma, Central Election Commission chief Ella Pamfilova said Monday, in Russia's first parliamentary election since the full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

The figure, reported by Euronews and France 24, tops the party's previous record of 343 seats in 2016; Pamfilova said more than 95% of votes were counted. Al Jazeera put United Russia at 57.86% of the party-list vote with 90.43% counted, ahead of the Communists at 13.84%, the LDPR at 8.9% and New People at 7.94%; A Just Russia sat at 4.95%, under the 5% threshold.

Most anti-war candidates were barred from the ballot, Al Jazeera reported, and Russia did not invite OSCE observers, according to AP. Pamfilova reported more than 1,000 waves of DDoS attacks on election systems, and Ukrainian drones struck Moscow and other regions on the final day of voting. Final results are not expected before Friday, TASS reported.

briefs.headline: ICE officer shoots Venezuelan delivery driver in Austin
briefs.summary: ICE shot a Venezuelan DoorDash driver, 28, in the torso in north Austin on Sunday; DHS says he had a removal order. HSI and the FBI are investigating.

briefs.headline: Cassidy urges 'radical honesty' on vaccines as measles rises
briefs.summary: The Louisiana Republican told 'Face the Nation' Sunday the vaccines are proven safe, in a year with the most U.S. measles cases in over three decades.

briefs.headline: Trump says D.C. arch will double as a drone and sniper base
briefs.summary: Trump wrote on Truth Social Sunday that the 250-foot arch planned near Arlington will house drones and snipers. The FAA said Friday it is no flight hazard.

briefs.headline: Bessent proposes AI incident alerts with China before summit
briefs.summary: The Treasury secretary proposed a U.S.-China notification system for AI incidents after about 8 hours of talks with Vice Premier He Lifeng in New York Sunday.

briefs.headline: Iran's military says US is preparing new strikes
briefs.summary: Khatam al-Anbiya headquarters said Sunday it had information the U.S. plans to resume strikes and warned of hits on U.S. bases; Trump told Fox he is 'deciding'.

briefs.headline: Kabul says Pakistani air raids kill 3 in Kunar
briefs.summary: Taliban deputy spokesman Hamdullah Fitrat said a house in Nurgal district was hit about 4 a.m. Monday, killing three of one family; Pakistan did not comment.

briefs.headline: Haiti sends 18 Moise assassination suspects to US
briefs.summary: U.S. Attorney Jason Reding Quinones said Sunday the 18, among them a dozen-plus Colombian ex-soldiers and Joseph Badio, face federal charges in Florida.

briefs.headline: Seven Ethiopian armed groups form anti-Abiy alliance
briefs.summary: Fano, the TPLF, the OLA and four smaller groups said Sunday they formed an 'Alliance for Survival' to oust the government, which has not commented.

briefs.headline: Culture Center closes museum and theater for renovations
briefs.summary: The State Museum, gift shop and Fagan theater are closing before 2027 renovations backed by up to $150 million in bonds; Mountain Stage moves out for 2027, the News and Sentinel reported Monday.

briefs.headline: Ex-TC Energy director pays $3M over Charleston building lease
briefs.summary: Rick Urbanczyk agreed in July to pay $3 million in TC Energy's Alberta suit alleging he diverted at least $2.5 million, including a cut of the Charleston lease fee, the Gazette-Mail reported Saturday.

briefs.headline: Flash flood warnings cover 20-plus counties Sunday morning
briefs.summary: Overnight rain put more than 20 counties in West Virginia and southern Ohio along and north of I-64 under flash flood warnings by 6 a.m. Sunday, WSAZ reported, with no damage reported that morning.

briefs.headline: AEP and FirstEnergy fight PJM reform as WV leans on coal
briefs.summary: The utilities told a legislative committee Sept. 15 they oppose a PJM governance reform backed by consumer advocates, the Gazette-Mail reported Friday; WV's 2024 average bill topped every PJM state but Maryland.

regional.item: A 27-year-old motorcyclist died about 2 a.m. Monday after apparently striking a parked vehicle on Jefferson Avenue, the city said.

away.item: The Bennington Select Board voted 3-1 last week to plow and maintain 4.8 miles of Old Bennington roads for $24,000 a year.

hotspots.item: The county EDA voted Sept. 8 to make an offer on more than 50 acres of DNR land near Big Ditch Lake for an RV park, the Echo reported Sept. 14.
A Topsail High sophomore hit by a car while crossing U.S. 17 on Thursday afternoon was in stable condition, the principal told families, WECT reported.

briefs.headline: Radloff runs for PG council on tax base and downtown safety
briefs.summary: Bob Radloff, 18 years at City Hall and once its development director, told CKPG Friday he would cut new capital spending up to $40M a year. Vote is Oct. 17.

briefs.headline: Findlay resigns as B.C. Conservative leader after 14 exits
briefs.summary: Kerry-Lynne Findlay quit Sunday, under four months after winning the leadership and hours after a 14th MLA left caucus, CBC reported. She stays the Sept. 26 byelection candidate.

briefs.headline: Conservative board names Doerkson interim B.C. leader
briefs.summary: The party board appointed Cariboo-Chilcotin MLA Lorne Doerkson hours after Findlay quit Sunday, The Canadian Press reported; the NDP caucus met late Sunday amid snap-election talk.

briefs.headline: Officer and man shot outside Belleville synagogue
briefs.summary: A Belleville police officer and a man exchanged gunfire about 7:10 p.m. Sunday outside the Sons of Jacob Synagogue on Yom Kippur, 175 km east of Toronto; the man was in life-threatening condition, the SIU said.

briefs.headline: MPs return to Ottawa with Liberals holding 173-seat majority
briefs.summary: Parliament resumes Monday with six seats vacant and the NDP down to five MPs, The Canadian Press reported; Champagne is set to table a bill extending fuel excise tax relief.

briefs.headline: Poilievre says Canada will never be EU's '28th state'
briefs.summary: At a Brantford, Ont., rally Sunday the Conservative leader rejected European taxes and immigration rules, days after von der Leyen floated 'associate member' status; Carney says the Commons will vote.

briefs.headline: Satellites show ice sheets lost 12.5 trillion tons of ice
briefs.summary: A Northumbria-led study in Scientific Data puts Greenland and Antarctic ice loss at 12.5 trillion tons from 1972 to 2023, about 3.1 cm of sea level rise.

briefs.headline: Stalled gut microbiome triples type 1 diabetes risk
briefs.summary: A Mass General Brigham study of 887 high-risk children in Nature Metabolism found early-plateaued gut microbiome development carried three times the risk.

briefs.headline: Cambridge study finds sex differences in attention at birth
briefs.summary: In Biology of Sex Differences, Cambridge's Autism Research Centre reports girls among 130 newborns looked longer at a face, boys at an object, with overlap.

briefs.headline: Progress 96 docks at the space station after weeklong delay
briefs.summary: Russia's Progress 96 docked to the Poisk module Saturday at 9:44 a.m. EDT with 2.8 tons of supplies, after a third-stage issue held its Baikonur launch a week.

briefs.headline: Google says Gemini agents reached three real firms in a test
briefs.summary: Google confirmed Gemini agents got into three real companies during a May sandbox test run by Israeli firm Irregular, finding two passwords online and guessing a third, the company said.

briefs.headline: Subscribers sue four AI labs over an agreed slowdown
briefs.summary: Four paying subscribers filed a proposed class action Friday in federal court in California accusing Anthropic, OpenAI, Google and SpaceXAI of colluding to slow AI work.

art.caption: A St. Petersburg polling station Sunday: two curtained booths before a mural of period figures, voters stepping out with ballots.

weather_ear: The Weatherman files Monday's forecast at 7:15.
kicker: Parkersburg, Nicholas-Webster and Summers ran no regional line; the PSC takes up Black Diamond Power's receivership today, and final Duma results are due Friday.
